mechanical.notes: 0 guard failures; boot/visibility/framing/interaction pass from both views; negative control 13/13 + PDU defect caught 4x; offline clean (orchestrator-verified: no fetch/XHR/WebSocket/Image/http, importmap -> ./vendor/three/, asset imports relative). THE HEADLINE: the scene did not need optimization — the COUNTER did, and a figure reported FOUR TIMES was wrong. The counter used a flat traverse and called every mesh a draw call (612), but the renderer emits 523: 87 meshes are HIDDEN (the six cabinets' unused door variants + the mesh door turned off in the hero) and a hidden mesh is skipped entirely. Root cause: counting what is easy to count, not what is being budgeted; it survived because the wrong number was ALSO comfortably under budget — an error that only manifests at a threshold is invisible until the day it matters. Corrected finals: 523/1200 draws (44%), 32156/200000 tris (16.1%). A 1.68x discrepancy between his own two counters was reconciled: InstancedMesh (used internally by closed assets for wheels/side-panels/yoke = 12992 instance triangles) is ONE draw but N triangles, so 19164 + 12992 = 32156 — the draws figure counts it once (right), triangles does not; this does NOT contradict the no-instancing rule (that applies to the six separate SCENE cabinets, not a closed asset's internals). FACETING measured in pixels (sagitta at dpr3 at each camera's real distance): all curved environment geometry < 1 px (hanging screens 0.52, detectors 0.76, bench legs 0.45), so with 84% of the triangle budget unspent the answer is NOT to raise tessellation — spending budget because it is available buys nothing. AND an optimization MEASURED and correctly DECLINED: 52% of raycast time is in invisible geometry (three r160 checks only `layers`, not `visible`, verified in the bundle), 0.341 ms/pick vs 0.162 — but against a 16.7 ms frame in a pointer event, it is 52% of something that does not matter, and the remedies (mirror visible->layers, or a cached pickable set) add state to resync on every toggle, and a stale cache is exactly the silent-failure class this run has spent seven passes eliminating. A remedy more fragile than the problem is not an optimization. Healthy sharing: 140 unique materials / 523 meshes, 151 meshes reuse geometry.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. A model optimization pass precisely because it optimizes almost nothing: it treats optimization as measurement in both directions and lands on the honest answers — correct the COUNTER not the scene (a draw figure reported four times was 612 when the renderer emits 523, because hidden meshes are not draw calls), do NOT raise tessellation (every curved face already sub-pixel), and do NOT detach the invisible raycast subtrees (52% of a cost that does not matter, bought with a stale-cache fragility worse than the problem). It also reconciled a 1.68x discrepancy between its own two counters before reporting — applying to itself the standard it had just applied to a counter that did not reconcile — and reported a closed-asset faceting finding without touching it. No regression, offline clean, negative control 13/13. Cleared to P6, the last gate of the run.
